subject: Throughput squeeze: Bluefin reserved capacity mismatch & GPU pool contention
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@bluefin-analytics.com>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@bluefin-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden drop in reserved throughput + latency/error spike

Hi team,

We started seeing a sustained increase in tail latency and 5xx errors for our reserved workloads this morning (approx 08:45 PST). Despite our committed throughput of 12k rps for the reserved pool, our observed sustained throughput is closer to 7k - requests are queuing and occasional token generation timeouts are happening.

Impact:
- Critical inference paths (customer scoring pipeline) are delayed by 800-1,200ms per request, causing downstream job failures.
- Error rate on model endpoint bluefin-prod/score-v2 jumped from ~0.2% to ~3.7%.
- Business impact: batch SLA at risk for two enterprise customers.

We attached the SLA usage report and a short snippet of request ids. Please advise immediate remediation steps and whether this is a pool saturation issue on Redwood's end or something we should change in our request patterns.

We need a timeline for mitigation and whether you will enable burst capacity or failover to hosted variants. This is hitting revenue-critical runs.

Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform, Bluefin Analytics
sanjay@bluefin-analytics.com

Attachments: SLA-usage-report-20270211.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, ops@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 07:12:30 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden drop in reserved throughput + latency/error spike

Thanks for the ping — I'm looking into this now. Initial telemetry shows:

- Dedicated pool for Bluefin (pool-id: dsp-us-west-2-07) shows average GPU util at 94% across nodes and a rising queue length starting 07:50 PST.
- KV cache hit rates for score-v2 are lower than baseline (likely caused by increased prefix variance).
- OOMs not observed, but GPU-side scheduling shows longer host->device transfer wait times consistent with contention.

Short-term mitigations I can trigger immediately (recommend implementing in order):
1) Temporarily allow burst to hosted capacity for non-sensitive routes (we have policy to keep PII lanes on dedicated). Will need Alex/Pricing signoff for credits if this extends beyond 2 hours.
2) Apply a rapid batching cap (reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 32) to lower per-request latency while we investigate throughput inefficiency.
3) Rolling restart of 3 nodes in the pool to restore scheduler balance (ETA 45m).

I'm opening INF-3491 with traces attached — please push logs/trace ids from the customer so I can correlate.

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

> On Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 09:36 AM Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 08:05:22 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden drop in reserved throughput + latency/error spike

Thanks Marissa — I reviewed the kernel-level traces Marissa uploaded to INF-3491 and correlated them with the throttle traces the customer shared. Key observations:

- We see significant tail latency introduced at the kernel enqueue path when multiple large-sequence requests overlap with a high kv-cache miss rate. This amplifies with our continuous-batching heuristic in the dedicated runtime.
- A recent scheduler tweak (deployed 2027-02-09) lowered the threshold for max inflight batches per GPU to prioritize latency for small-sequence traffic; unintended side-effect: heavier long-seq workloads monopolize available inflight slots, reducing effective reserved throughput for Bluefin's long-sequence scoring jobs.

Proposed immediate plan (engineering):
- Revert the scheduler threshold to previous value for dsp-us-west-2-07 (hotfix) — rollout target: 30m after approval.
- Apply Marissa's rolling-restart and batching cap in tandem to reduce queuing pressure.
- If hotfix is insufficient, enable temporary progressive routing: route 20% of traffic to hosted variants with matched quantized model (non-PII).

I'll prepare a short playbook with exact rollback commands. Attaching throttle_trace-20270212.log for the team.

Rishi
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime

Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Bluefin incident: proposed customer comm and credit recommendation

Team — looping in finance and product execs. Bluefin (DB-8421) is experiencing reserved throughput shortfalls due to dedicated pool contention. Rishi and Marissa have a remediation plan (hotfix + rolling restart + batching cap) that should restore effective throughput within ~1–2 hours of execution.

Customer impact: one of Bluefin's enterprise scoring jobs may miss SLAs if not mitigated within the next two hours. Proposed customer-facing items:
- Immediate: acknowledge and notify customer of mitigation steps (hotfix + restart); promise hourly status updates.
- Near-term: enable 20% progressive routing to hosted variant where allowed (non-PII).
- Commercial remediation: offer a pro-rated service credit equal to 10% of February reserved commitment if we miss the SLA for more than one billing window.

Ben, draft the customer email (we should be transparent, own the impact, and provide an ETA). Finance: confirm credit mechanism and whether 10% is acceptable as standard escalation.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Success & Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick triage and the detailed plan. A few asks from our side:

- Please confirm whether the hotfix will require any client-side changes (we prefer zero-touch on our end).
- If you enable routing to hosted variants, we need a clear rollback and data exposure assessment — ensure non-PII enforcement is active.
- We'd like daily status emails until the baseline throughput stabilizes and a post-mortem including root cause and mitigation timeline.

We appreciate the credit offer; once the technical fix is stable we'll sync on formal commercial remediation.

Sanjay
